text: For a geometric theory $\mathbb{T}$, the classifying topos $\mathrm{Set}[\mathbb{T}]$ is characterized, for every topos $\mathcal{E}$, by which correspondence?
choices: Objects of $\mathcal{E}$ correspond to points of $\mathrm{Set}[\mathbb{T}]$
Subobjects in $\mathcal{E}$ correspond to open sets of $\mathrm{Set}[\mathbb{T}]$
Topos morphisms $\mathcal{E}\to\mathrm{Set}[\mathbb{T}]$ correspond to models of $\mathbb{T}$ in $\mathcal{E}$
Functors $\mathrm{Set}[\mathbb{T}]\to\mathcal{E}$ correspond to models of $\mathbb{T}$ in $\mathbf{Set}$
explanation: The defining universal property is 'Topos morphisms $\mathcal{E}\to\mathrm{Set}[\mathbb{T}]\cong$ models of $\mathbb{T}$ in $\mathcal{E}$,' so the classifying topos represents all models of $\mathbb{T}$. The other options reverse the direction of the morphisms or swap 'models in $\mathcal{E}$' for unrelated data such as points, subobjects, or models in $\mathbf{Set}$.
